sections.title: The octet rule and the two routes to a full shell

board_events.text: Every atom wants a full outer shell
Octet rule: reach 8 valence electrons (2 for H and He).
Two honest routes: TRANSFER electrons, or SHARE them.
Transfer gives ionic bond; sharing gives covalent bond.
Kossel explained transfer; Lewis explained sharing.

board_events.text: Opposite ions cling by electrostatic attraction.
Covalent bond: both atoms pool a shared pair between them.

segments.text: <curious>Here is the one idea the whole chapter hangs on.</curious> Every atom, the moment it forms, behaves like a tired commuter hunting for a comfortable seat, and for an atom that comfortable seat is a full outermost shell.

For most elements a comfortable shell means eight valence electrons, and for the tiny ones, hydrogen and helium, just two is enough. We call this the octet rule, and almost all of bonding is atoms scrambling to reach that settled, noble gas arrangement.

There are exactly two honest ways to get there. An atom can give away or take electrons outright, a clean transfer of ownership, or it can share electrons with a neighbour, like two students splitting the cost of a single textbook so both can read it.
The transfer route gives you the ionic bond, and the sharing route gives you the covalent bond. Hold on to that single split, because every other idea in the chapter branches off from it.
Walther Kossel worked out the transfer story and Gilbert Lewis worked out the sharing story, and together they form what we call the Kossel Lewis approach to bonding.

Lewis also handed us a lovely bookkeeping trick: write the symbol and place its valence electrons as dots around it. Sodium has one lonely dot, chlorine has seven and is one short of a full set, so sodium simply hands its single electron over.

Now sodium is a positive ion and chlorine a negative ion, and the two opposite charges snap together by pure electrostatic attraction, exactly like two magnets. Scale that clinging across an entire crystal and you feel it as the strength of common salt.

The covalent bond is a different animal. Nobody surrenders ownership; both atoms push their electrons into a shared pair that sits between them. An ionic bond is a sale, but a covalent bond is a genuine joint venture where the capital stays pooled.

<curious>पूरा chapter बस एक idea पर टिका है।</curious> हर atom बनते ही ऐसा behave करता है जैसे कोई थका हुआ passenger comfortable seat ढूँढ रहा हो, और atom के लिए वो seat है एक भरा हुआ outermost shell।

ज़्यादातर elements के लिए comfortable shell का मतलब है eight valence electrons, और छोटे वाले hydrogen और helium के लिए सिर्फ़ two ही काफ़ी हैं। इसी को octet rule कहते हैं, और लगभग सारी bonding इसी stable noble gas arrangement को पाने की कोशिश है।

वहाँ पहुँचने के exactly दो honest तरीके हैं। atom या तो electrons पूरी तरह दे या ले सकता है, यानी clean transfer of ownership, या फिर neighbour के साथ electrons share कर सकता है, जैसे दो students एक ही textbook का खर्च बाँट लें।
Transfer वाला route देता है ionic bond, और sharing वाला route देता है covalent bond। इस एक फ़र्क़ को पकड़ के रखिए, क्योंकि chapter के बाक़ी सारे ideas यहीं से निकलते हैं।
Walther Kossel ने transfer की कहानी समझाई और Gilbert Lewis ने sharing की, और मिलकर ये दोनों बनाते हैं वो चीज़ जिसे हम bonding का Kossel Lewis approach कहते हैं।

Lewis ने एक प्यारा सा bookkeeping trick भी दिया: symbol लिखो और valence electrons को dots की तरह चारों तरफ़ रख दो। Sodium के पास एक अकेला dot है, chlorine के पास seven और वो one short है, तो sodium बस अपना अकेला electron दे देता है।

अब sodium positive ion है और chlorine negative ion, और दोनों opposite charges pure electrostatic attraction से snap हो जाते हैं, बिलकुल दो magnets की तरह। इसी clinging को पूरे crystal में फैला दो तो यही common salt की मज़बूती बन जाती है।

Covalent bond एक अलग ही जानवर है। यहाँ कोई ownership नहीं छोड़ता, दोनों atoms अपने electrons को एक shared pair में डाल देते हैं जो बीच में बैठती है। Ionic bond एक sale है, पर covalent bond एक असली joint venture है जहाँ capital pool में रहता है।

sections.title: Polar bonds, dipole moment, and why symmetry cancels

board_events.text: Sharing is rarely perfectly equal
Lopsided sharing = a polar bond.
Bond dipoles add like VECTORS.
Symmetric molecule can have polar bonds yet zero net dipole.
CO2 is non-polar; water is polar.
The octet rule is a guide, not an iron law.
Fails for: electron-deficient, expanded-octet, odd-electron.
Lewis maps connectivity, not shape or energy.

segments.text: Real sharing is almost never a perfect fifty fifty. The greedier partner, the more electronegative atom, pulls the shared pair closer to its own side, leaving that end slightly negative and the other end slightly positive.

That lopsided sharing is exactly what we call a polar bond. It behaves like a tiny tug of war rope with a small plus charge at one end and a small minus charge at the other, and the measure of that lopsidedness is the dipole moment.

Here is the crucial subtlety: if a molecule has several such tug of war ropes pulling in different directions, what matters is the net pull. And because these pulls are vectors, they can add up, or they can cancel out completely.

Picture three people pulling a ring outward at one hundred twenty degrees to each other, which is the shape of boron trifluoride. Each pulls hard, yet the ring does not move at all, because the three pulls cancel by symmetry.

This single idea, that bond dipoles add like vectors, explains why carbon dioxide is non polar while water is not. Carbon dioxide is linear, so its two bond dipoles point in exactly opposite directions and cancel, but water is bent, so its two pulls do not.
One honest warning before we move on. The octet rule is a wonderfully useful guide, not an iron law, and it fails in three clear families of molecules that the exams love to test.

It fails for electron deficient molecules like beryllium chloride and boron trichloride, where the central atom is happy with fewer than eight. It fails for expanded octet species like sulphur hexafluoride and phosphorus pentachloride, where third period atoms exceed eight. And it fails for odd electron molecules like nitric oxide, which simply cannot pair everything up.

So treat a Lewis structure as a faithful map of connectivity and electron count, never as a map of geometry or of why a bond forms energetically. For shape and for energy we will need V S E P R, valence bond theory, and molecular orbital theory in the coming sections.

असली sharing कभी perfect fifty fifty नहीं होती। ज़्यादा लालची partner, यानी more electronegative atom, shared pair को अपनी तरफ़ खींच लेता है, जिससे वो end थोड़ा negative और दूसरा end थोड़ा positive हो जाता है।

इसी lopsided sharing को हम polar bond कहते हैं। ये एक छोटी सी tug of war rope की तरह behave करती है जिसके एक end पर छोटा सा plus charge और दूसरे पर छोटा सा minus charge होता है, और इस lopsidedness का measure है dipole moment।

यहाँ एक ज़रूरी subtlety है: अगर किसी molecule में ऐसी कई tug of war ropes अलग अलग directions में खींच रही हैं, तो मायने रखता है net pull। और चूँकि ये pulls vectors हैं, ये add भी हो सकते हैं और पूरी तरह cancel भी हो सकते हैं।

सोचिए तीन लोग एक ring को एक दूसरे से one hundred twenty degrees पर बाहर की ओर खींच रहे हैं, जो boron trifluoride की shape है। हर कोई ज़ोर से खींच रहा है, फिर भी ring बिलकुल नहीं हिलती, क्योंकि तीनों pulls symmetry से cancel हो जाते हैं।

यही एक idea, कि bond dipoles vectors की तरह add होते हैं, समझा देता है कि carbon dioxide non polar क्यों है जबकि water नहीं। Carbon dioxide linear है, तो इसके दो bond dipoles बिलकुल opposite directions में point करके cancel हो जाते हैं, पर water bent है, तो इसके दो pulls cancel नहीं होते।
आगे बढ़ने से पहले एक honest warning। Octet rule एक बहुत useful guide है, कोई iron law नहीं, और ये molecules की तीन clear families में fail करता है जिन्हें exams टेस्ट करना बहुत पसंद करते हैं।

ये fail करता है electron deficient molecules के लिए जैसे beryllium chloride और boron trichloride, जहाँ central atom eight से कम में ही खुश है। ये fail करता है expanded octet species के लिए जैसे sulphur hexafluoride और phosphorus pentachloride, जहाँ third period atoms eight से आगे निकल जाते हैं। और ये fail करता है odd electron molecules के लिए जैसे nitric oxide, जो सब कुछ pair ही नहीं कर पाता।

तो Lewis structure को connectivity और electron count का एक faithful map मानिए, कभी भी geometry का या ये समझने का map मत मानिए कि bond energetically क्यों बनता है। Shape और energy के लिए हमें आगे के sections में V S E P R, valence bond theory, और molecular orbital theory चाहिए होंगे।

sections.title: Formal charge, bond order, and bond parameters

board_events.text: The bookkeeping quantities of bonding
Formal charges must sum to the species charge.
Bond order (Lewis): shared pairs between two atoms.
Bond order up: bond enthalpy up, bond length down.
Bond enthalpy: energy to break one mole of a bond (gas).
Lattice enthalpy: energy released forming solid from gas ions.

segments.text: Bonding has few derivations in the physics sense; what it rewards is disciplined bookkeeping. Let us collect the key quantities, starting with the one the exams test most, the formal charge.

Formal charge is the hypothetical charge an atom appears to carry if every shared pair were split exactly down the middle. It equals V, the valence electrons of the free neutral atom, minus L, the lone pair electrons on the atom, minus half of B, the bonding electrons around it.
There is a built in check you should always use: the formal charges on all the atoms must add up to the overall charge of the species. If they do not, you have miscounted somewhere.

Next is bond order. In the Lewis sense it is just the number of shared electron pairs between two bonded atoms, so a single bond is one, a double is two, a triple is three. Isoelectronic species share the same bond order, which is why nitrogen, carbon monoxide, and the nitric oxide cation all have bond order three.
Remember the trend that ties everything together: as bond order rises, bond enthalpy rises and bond length falls. Higher bond order means the atoms are pulled together harder and held more tightly.

Bond length is the equilibrium internuclear distance between two bonded atoms, measured in picometres, where one angstrom equals one hundred picometres. For a covalent bond between A and B it is simply the sum of the two covalent radii, r A plus r B.

Bond enthalpy is the energy in kilojoules per mole needed to break one mole of a particular bond in the gaseous state. When a polyatomic molecule has several identical bonds, we report the average, or mean, bond enthalpy.

Finally, lattice enthalpy is the energy released when one mole of an ionic solid forms from its gaseous ions. It is larger for ions of higher charge and smaller size, and it is the quantity that decides whether an ionic crystal forms readily at all.

Bonding में physics वाले derivations कम हैं; ये जो चीज़ reward करती है वो है disciplined bookkeeping। चलिए key quantities इकट्ठा करते हैं, शुरू करते हैं उससे जिसे exams सबसे ज़्यादा टेस्ट करते हैं, formal charge।

Formal charge वो hypothetical charge है जो atom तब carry करता दिखता है जब हर shared pair बिलकुल बीच से बाँट दी जाए। ये equal होता है V यानी free neutral atom के valence electrons, minus L यानी atom पर lone pair electrons, minus half of B यानी उसके चारों ओर bonding electrons।
एक built in check है जो आपको हमेशा use करना चाहिए: सारे atoms के formal charges जुड़कर species के overall charge के बराबर होने चाहिए। अगर नहीं होते, तो कहीं miscount हुआ है।

अगला है bond order। Lewis sense में ये बस दो bonded atoms के बीच shared electron pairs की संख्या है, तो single bond one है, double two, triple three। Isoelectronic species का bond order same होता है, इसीलिए nitrogen, carbon monoxide, और nitric oxide cation सबका bond order three है।

वो trend याद रखिए जो सब कुछ जोड़ता है: जैसे जैसे bond order बढ़ता है, bond enthalpy बढ़ती है और bond length घटती है। ज़्यादा bond order का मतलब atoms एक दूसरे की ओर ज़्यादा ज़ोर से खिंचते हैं और ज़्यादा tightly पकड़े रहते हैं।

Bond length दो bonded atoms के बीच की equilibrium internuclear distance है, picometres में मापी जाती है, जहाँ one angstrom equals one hundred picometres। A और B के बीच covalent bond के लिए ये बस दोनों covalent radii का sum है, r A plus r B।

Bond enthalpy वो energy है, kilojoules per mole में, जो gaseous state में एक particular bond के one mole को तोड़ने के लिए चाहिए। जब किसी polyatomic molecule में कई identical bonds हों, तो हम average, यानी mean bond enthalpy report करते हैं।

आख़िर में, lattice enthalpy वो energy है जो तब release होती है जब एक ionic solid का one mole अपने gaseous ions से बनता है। ये higher charge और smaller size वाले ions के लिए बड़ी होती है, और यही तय करती है कि ionic crystal आसानी से बनेगा भी या नहीं।

sections.title: Dipole moment and percentage ionic character

board_events.text: Measuring how lopsided a bond really is
SI unit coulomb-metre; practical unit debye.
Net molecular dipole = vector sum of bond dipoles.
No bond is purely ionic or purely covalent.
e times 100 pm is about 4.8 D (mental yardstick).

segments.text: We said a polar bond is lopsided sharing; now let us put a number on that lopsidedness. That number is the dipole moment, written with the Greek letter mu.

The dipole moment equals q, the magnitude of the charge separation, times d, the distance between the centres of positive and negative charge. It is a vector, and by convention it points from the plus end to the minus end.
The S I unit is the coulomb metre, but that is an inconveniently large unit for molecules, so in practice we use the debye.
One debye equals three point three three six times ten to the minus thirty coulomb metres. Keep this conversion factor at your fingertips, because every percentage ionic character problem needs it.

For a whole molecule, the net dipole is the vector sum of all the individual bond dipoles. This is the formula behind everything we said about symmetry: symmetric arrangements let the bond dipoles cancel to a net of zero.

Now a beautiful idea. No real bond is purely ionic or purely covalent; every bond sits somewhere in between. We estimate the ionic share by comparing the real, observed dipole moment with the value it would have if the electron were transferred completely.

Percentage ionic character is the observed dipole divided by the fully ionic dipole, times one hundred, where the fully ionic dipole is the electronic charge e times the bond length d. Since real sharing is only partial, the observed value is always smaller than the fully ionic one.

<whisper>Here is a speed secret worth memorising.</whisper> The electronic charge times one hundred picometres is about four point eight debye. Scale it linearly with bond length and you can estimate the fully ionic dipole in your head, no calculator needed.
हमने कहा था polar bond एक lopsided sharing है; अब उस lopsidedness पर एक number रखते हैं। वो number है dipole moment, जिसे Greek letter mu से लिखते हैं।

Dipole moment equal होता है q यानी charge separation के magnitude, times d यानी positive और negative charge के centres के बीच की distance। ये एक vector है, और convention से ये plus end से minus end की ओर point करता है।
S I unit है coulomb metre, पर molecules के लिए ये असुविधाजनक रूप से बड़ी unit है, इसलिए practice में हम debye use करते हैं।
One debye equals three point three three six times ten to the power minus thirty coulomb metres। इस conversion factor को उँगलियों पर रखिए, क्योंकि हर percentage ionic character problem में ये चाहिए।

पूरे molecule के लिए, net dipole सारे individual bond dipoles का vector sum होता है। यही वो formula है जो symmetry के बारे में हमारी सारी बातों के पीछे है: symmetric arrangements में bond dipoles cancel होकर net zero दे देते हैं।

अब एक ख़ूबसूरत idea। कोई भी real bond न पूरी तरह ionic होता है न पूरी तरह covalent; हर bond कहीं बीच में बैठता है। हम ionic share का अंदाज़ा real, observed dipole moment की तुलना उस value से करके लगाते हैं जो electron पूरी तरह transfer होने पर होती।

Percentage ionic character है observed dipole divided by fully ionic dipole, times one hundred, जहाँ fully ionic dipole electronic charge e times bond length d है। चूँकि real sharing सिर्फ़ partial होती है, observed value हमेशा fully ionic value से छोटी होती है।

<whisper>एक speed secret जो याद रखने लायक़ है।</whisper> electronic charge times one hundred picometres लगभग four point eight debye होता है। इसे bond length के साथ linearly scale कीजिए और आप fully ionic dipole दिमाग़ में ही estimate कर सकते हैं, बिना calculator के।

sections.title: Drawing Lewis structures and assigning formal charge

board_events.text: A disciplined five-step procedure
Step 1: Count total valence electrons (adjust for charge).
Step 2: Pick the central atom (least electronegative, never H).
Step 3: Single bonds, then lone pairs to outer atoms first.
Step 4: Make multiple bonds if the centre is short.
Step 5: Verify octets and compute formal charges.
Half of B because the other half belongs to the partner.
Best structure: FC nearest zero; minus on most electronegative atom.

segments.text: <curious>How do you actually draw a Lewis structure without guessing?</curious> There is a disciplined five step recipe that never fails if you follow it in order.

Step one, count the total valence electrons by adding up the valence electrons of every atom. For an anion add one electron for each unit of negative charge, and for a cation subtract one for each unit of positive charge.

Step two, pick the central atom. Usually the least electronegative atom sits in the centre, and it is never hydrogen, because the central atom is the one most willing to share its electrons out in several directions.

Step three, connect everything with single bonds, then distribute the remaining electrons as lone pairs. Fill the outer atoms to a full octet first, and only afterwards place any leftover electrons on the central atom.

Step four, if the central atom is still short of an octet, make multiple bonds by converting a lone pair on an adjacent atom into a shared double or triple bond. Sharing more pairs is how an electron starved centre reaches eight without inventing electrons that do not exist.
Step five, verify. Check every octet and compute the formal charge on each atom. The very act of assigning formal charge tells you whether your structure is the best one.

When you apply the formal charge formula, understand each term. You start from what the atom owns when neutral, that is V; you keep full credit for its lone pairs L; but you get credit for only half of every shared pair, because the other half belongs to the bonding partner.

The best Lewis structure is the one whose formal charges are closest to zero, with any negative formal charge sitting on the most electronegative atom. That single principle picks the winning structure whenever several are possible.
<curious>बिना अंदाज़ा लगाए Lewis structure असल में कैसे बनाते हैं?</curious> एक disciplined पाँच step वाली recipe है जो अगर order में follow करें तो कभी fail नहीं होती।
Step one, हर atom के valence electrons जोड़कर total valence electrons count कीजिए। Anion के लिए हर unit negative charge पर एक electron जोड़िए, और cation के लिए हर unit positive charge पर एक घटाइए।

Step two, central atom चुनिए। आम तौर पर सबसे कम electronegative atom बीच में बैठता है, और ये कभी hydrogen नहीं होता, क्योंकि central atom वही होता है जो कई directions में अपने electrons share करने को सबसे ज़्यादा तैयार हो।
Step three, सब कुछ single bonds से जोड़िए, फिर बचे हुए electrons को lone pairs की तरह बाँटिए। पहले outer atoms का पूरा octet भरिए, और उसके बाद ही कोई बचा हुआ electron central atom पर रखिए।

Step four, अगर central atom अब भी octet से कम है, तो किसी adjacent atom की lone pair को shared double या triple bond में बदलकर multiple bonds बनाइए। ज़्यादा pairs share करना ही वो तरीक़ा है जिससे electron starved centre बिना नए electrons invent किए eight तक पहुँचता है।
Step five, verify कीजिए। हर octet check कीजिए और हर atom पर formal charge निकालिए। formal charge assign करने का यही काम बता देता है कि आपकी structure सबसे अच्छी है या नहीं।

जब आप formal charge formula लगाएँ, हर term को समझिए। आप शुरू करते हैं उससे जो atom neutral होने पर owns करता है, यानी V; उसकी lone pairs L का पूरा credit रखते हैं; पर हर shared pair का सिर्फ़ आधा credit मिलता है, क्योंकि बाक़ी आधा bonding partner का होता है।

सबसे अच्छी Lewis structure वो है जिसके formal charges zero के सबसे क़रीब हों, और कोई भी negative formal charge सबसे electronegative atom पर बैठा हो। यही एक principle जब कई structures possible हों तो winning structure चुन देता है।

board_events.text: Step A: sublimation of the metal (solid to gas atoms).
Step B: ionise the metal; Step C: break half the non-metal bond.
Step D: electron gain by the non-metal (energy returned).
Step E: gaseous ions collapse into the crystal (lattice enthalpy).
Stability = energy invested vs energy returned.

segments.text: Lattice enthalpy cannot be measured directly, because you cannot simply watch gaseous ions collapse into a crystal in a calorimeter. So we get it indirectly, using Hess's law.

Hess's law says the total enthalpy change of a reaction is independent of the path taken. So if we build a closed cycle from the elements to the ionic solid by two different routes, the two routes must give the same total, and that lets us solve for the one unknown.

Here is the closed cycle for a salt M X, such as an alkali halide. The direct route is the formation enthalpy from the elements straight down to the solid. The alternative route goes the long way around, through five separate steps, and the two must balance.
The long route begins by subliming the metal, turning solid metal into gaseous atoms; that is the sublimation enthalpy, and it costs energy.

Next the metal atom is ionised, losing an electron to become a positive ion, which costs the ionisation enthalpy. In parallel, half the bond dissociation enthalpy is spent to split the non metal molecule into single gaseous atoms.

Now the non metal atom grabs that electron to become a negative ion, releasing the electron gain enthalpy. So far we have spent energy subliming, ionising, and breaking bonds, and only begun to get some back.

Finally the gaseous positive and negative ions collapse into the crystal lattice, and this last step releases the lattice enthalpy, the single quantity we were after. Setting the two paths equal lets us solve for it cleanly.

The physical takeaway is worth carrying away. A crystal's stability is a balance sheet, energy invested in sublimation, ionisation, and bond breaking, set against energy returned by electron gain and lattice formation. When the lattice enthalpy is large enough, favoured by small, highly charged ions, the ionic solid forms readily.
Lattice enthalpy को सीधे नहीं माप सकते, क्योंकि आप calorimeter में gaseous ions को crystal में गिरते देख नहीं सकते। इसलिए हम इसे indirectly निकालते हैं, Hess's law की मदद से।

Hess's law कहता है कि किसी reaction का total enthalpy change इस बात पर निर्भर नहीं करता कि रास्ता कौन सा लिया। तो अगर हम elements से ionic solid तक दो अलग रास्तों से एक closed cycle बनाएँ, दोनों रास्तों का total same होना चाहिए, और यही हमें एक unknown निकालने देता है।

यहाँ एक salt M X के लिए closed cycle है, जैसे कोई alkali halide। Direct route है formation enthalpy, elements से सीधे नीचे solid तक। Alternative route लंबे रास्ते से जाता है, पाँच अलग steps से होकर, और दोनों को balance होना है।
लंबा route शुरू होता है metal को subliming करके, solid metal को gaseous atoms में बदलकर; ये sublimation enthalpy है, और इसमें energy लगती है।

फिर metal atom को ionise किया जाता है, एक electron खोकर positive ion बनता है, जिसमें ionisation enthalpy लगती है। साथ ही, non metal molecule को single gaseous atoms में तोड़ने के लिए आधी bond dissociation enthalpy ख़र्च होती है।

अब non metal atom वो electron पकड़कर negative ion बनता है, electron gain enthalpy release करता है। अब तक हमने subliming, ionising, और bonds तोड़ने में energy ख़र्च की है, और अभी थोड़ी वापस मिलनी शुरू ही हुई है।

आख़िर में gaseous positive और negative ions crystal lattice में गिरते हैं, और यही आख़िरी step lattice enthalpy release करता है, वही एक quantity जिसकी हमें तलाश थी। दोनों paths को बराबर रखकर हम इसे साफ़ साफ़ solve कर लेते हैं।

Physical takeaway साथ ले जाने लायक़ है। किसी crystal की stability एक balance sheet है, sublimation, ionisation, और bond breaking में लगाई गई energy, electron gain और lattice formation से लौटी energy के मुक़ाबले। जब lattice enthalpy काफ़ी बड़ी हो, जो small और highly charged ions से favour होती है, तो ionic solid आसानी से बन जाता है।

segments.text: <curious>Let us put the recipe to work on ozone.</curious> The task is to draw the Lewis structure of the ozone molecule and calculate the formal charge on each of its three oxygen atoms. This is a classic C B S E board level question.
Start with the electron count. Three oxygen atoms, each with six valence electrons, give a total of eighteen valence electrons to place.

A satisfactory structure has a central oxygen double bonded to one terminal oxygen and single bonded to the other, with lone pairs completing every octet. The central oxygen carries one lone pair, the double bonded terminal carries two, and the single bonded terminal carries three.
Now apply the formal charge formula to each oxygen, with V equal to six throughout since they are all oxygen. We just need L and B for each atom.

The central oxygen has two lone pair electrons and six bonding electrons, since one double plus one single bond is three shared pairs. So its formal charge is six minus two minus three, which is plus one.
The double bonded terminal oxygen has four lone pair electrons and four bonding electrons, so its formal charge is six minus four minus two, which is exactly zero.
The single bonded terminal oxygen has six lone pair electrons and only two bonding electrons, so its formal charge is six minus six minus one, which is minus one.

And now the built in check pays off: plus one, plus zero, plus minus one adds to zero, which matches the neutral ozone molecule. Our formal charges are plus one, zero, and minus one. Whenever the sum matches the molecular charge, you can trust the structure.

<curious>चलिए recipe को ozone पर लगाते हैं।</curious> काम है ozone molecule की Lewis structure बनाना और इसके तीनों oxygen atoms पर formal charge निकालना। ये एक classic C B S E board level question है।
Electron count से शुरू करते हैं। तीन oxygen atoms, हर एक के six valence electrons के साथ, total eighteen valence electrons देते हैं जिन्हें रखना है।

एक satisfactory structure में central oxygen एक terminal oxygen से double bonded और दूसरे से single bonded होता है, और lone pairs हर octet पूरा करती हैं। Central oxygen पर one lone pair, double bonded terminal पर two, और single bonded terminal पर three lone pairs होती हैं।
अब हर oxygen पर formal charge formula लगाइए, V हर जगह six के बराबर क्योंकि सब oxygen हैं। हमें बस हर atom के लिए L और B चाहिए।

Central oxygen पर two lone pair electrons और six bonding electrons हैं, क्योंकि one double plus one single bond मिलाकर three shared pairs हैं। तो इसका formal charge है six minus two minus three, यानी plus one।
Double bonded terminal oxygen पर four lone pair electrons और four bonding electrons हैं, तो इसका formal charge है six minus four minus two, यानी बिलकुल zero।
Single bonded terminal oxygen पर six lone pair electrons और सिर्फ़ two bonding electrons हैं, तो इसका formal charge है six minus six minus one, यानी minus one।

और अब built in check काम आता है: plus one, zero, और minus one मिलकर zero देते हैं, जो neutral ozone molecule से match करता है। हमारे formal charges हैं plus one, zero, और minus one। जब भी sum molecular charge से match करे, आप structure पर भरोसा कर सकते हैं।

sections.title: Worked examples: polarity by symmetry and percent ionic character

board_events.text: Two speed skills: spot the polar one, then quantify it
Q1: three of CCl4, BF3, CHCl3, CO2 are non-polar. Find the polar one.
CCl4 tetrahedral, BF3 planar, CO2 linear: all cancel.
Answer: CHCl3 is polar (symmetry broken).
Q2: bond length 130 pm, mu = 1.10 D. Find % ionic character.
Convert to debye: about 6.24 D.

segments.text: This section pairs two exam favourites. First a N E E T speed trap about polarity, then a J E E Main calculation of percentage ionic character. Together they cover the qualitative eye and the quantitative hand.

The first question gives four molecules, carbon tetrachloride, boron trifluoride, chloroform, and carbon dioxide, and tells us three have zero net dipole. We must find the single polar one. The speed rule: do not calculate anything, just ask whether symmetry lets the bond dipoles cancel.

Carbon tetrachloride has four identical dipoles pointing to the corners of a tetrahedron, so they cancel. Boron trifluoride has three identical dipoles at one hundred twenty degrees in a plane, so they cancel. Carbon dioxide has two equal, opposite dipoles in a straight line, so they cancel too.

So the answer is chloroform. Replacing just one chlorine of carbon tetrachloride with a hydrogen breaks the symmetry, and now the dipoles no longer cancel. The trap is thinking that four polar bonds behave the same in both molecules; it is the symmetry of the arrangement, not the mere presence of polar bonds, that decides polarity.

Now the second question. A diatomic molecule X Y has a bond length of one hundred thirty picometres and an observed dipole moment of one point one zero debye. We estimate its percentage ionic character, taking the electronic charge as one point six times ten to the minus nineteen coulombs.

Step one, the fully ionic dipole is the electronic charge times the bond length in metres. That is one point six times ten to the minus nineteen, times one hundred thirty times ten to the minus twelve, which comes to about two point zero eight times ten to the minus twenty nine coulomb metres.
Step two, convert that to debye by dividing by three point three three six times ten to the minus thirty. That gives about six point two four debye for the fully ionic value.

Step three, take the ratio: one point one zero divided by six point two four, times one hundred, gives about seventeen point six percent. So the bond is roughly eighteen percent ionic, predominantly covalent with a modest charge separation. A sanity check to remember: the observed value must always be smaller than the fully ionic value; if your ratio ever exceeds one hundred percent, you have slipped a power of ten in the bond length.

ये section दो exam favourites को जोड़ता है। पहले polarity पर एक N E E T speed trap, फिर percentage ionic character की एक J E E Main calculation। दोनों मिलकर qualitative नज़र और quantitative हाथ, दोनों cover करते हैं।

पहला सवाल चार molecules देता है, carbon tetrachloride, boron trifluoride, chloroform, और carbon dioxide, और बताता है कि तीन का net dipole zero है। हमें अकेला polar वाला ढूँढना है। Speed rule: कुछ भी calculate मत कीजिए, बस पूछिए कि symmetry bond dipoles को cancel होने देती है या नहीं।

Carbon tetrachloride में चार identical dipoles एक tetrahedron के corners की ओर point करते हैं, तो वो cancel हो जाते हैं। Boron trifluoride में तीन identical dipoles एक plane में one hundred twenty degrees पर हैं, तो वो cancel हो जाते हैं। Carbon dioxide में दो equal, opposite dipoles एक straight line में हैं, तो वो भी cancel हो जाते हैं।

तो answer है chloroform। Carbon tetrachloride के सिर्फ़ एक chlorine को hydrogen से बदलने पर symmetry टूट जाती है, और अब dipoles cancel नहीं होते। Trap ये सोचना है कि चार polar bonds दोनों molecules में एक जैसे behave करते हैं; polarity तय करती है arrangement की symmetry, ना कि सिर्फ़ polar bonds का होना।

अब दूसरा सवाल। एक diatomic molecule X Y का bond length one hundred thirty picometres है और observed dipole moment one point one zero debye। हम इसका percentage ionic character estimate करते हैं, electronic charge को one point six times ten to the power minus nineteen coulombs लेकर।

Step one, fully ionic dipole electronic charge times bond length in metres है। यानी one point six times ten to the power minus nineteen, times one hundred thirty times ten to the power minus twelve, जो लगभग two point zero eight times ten to the power minus twenty nine coulomb metres आता है।
Step two, इसे debye में बदलिए three point three three six times ten to the power minus thirty से divide करके। ये fully ionic value के लिए लगभग six point two four debye देता है।

Step three, ratio लीजिए: one point one zero divided by six point two four, times one hundred, लगभग seventeen point six percent देता है। तो bond क़रीब eighteen percent ionic है, ज़्यादातर covalent एक modest charge separation के साथ। एक sanity check याद रखिए: observed value हमेशा fully ionic value से छोटी होनी चाहिए; अगर ratio कभी one hundred percent से ऊपर जाए, तो आपने bond length में एक power of ten खिसका दिया है।

segments.text: This is a J E E Advanced level problem that ties formal charge to resonance. The azide ion is linear and symmetric, and we must draw a low formal charge structure, assign the charges, and use resonance to predict the two nitrogen nitrogen bond orders and lengths.
First the electron count. Three nitrogens give fifteen, and the single negative charge adds one, for sixteen valence electrons in total.

The lowest formal charge linear structure places two nitrogen nitrogen double bonds on the central nitrogen, with two lone pairs on each terminal nitrogen and none on the centre. Draw the whole thing bracketed with an overall minus one charge.

For formal charges, V is five throughout. The central nitrogen has no lone pairs and eight bonding electrons from its two double bonds, so its formal charge is five minus zero minus four, which is plus one.

Each terminal nitrogen has four lone pair electrons and four bonding electrons, so its formal charge is five minus four minus two, which is minus one. The sum, minus one plus one minus one, equals minus one, matching the ion's charge. The structure checks out.

Now resonance. This symmetric form has an equivalent partner in which the double bonds are redistributed into a triple bond on one side and a single bond on the other, and there is a mirror image partner with the arrangement reversed.

Because these two end on triple bond forms are equivalent and contribute equally, the real ion is the symmetric blend of all of them. Each nitrogen nitrogen linkage ends up with an average bond order of two.

And here is the deep lesson of resonance: the two nitrogen nitrogen bonds are identical in length, there is no longer bond and no shorter bond. The molecule is a single blended species, like a chutney rather than a switch flicking between two recipes, so partial bond orders and equal bond lengths emerge naturally, a conclusion no single Lewis structure could ever deliver.

ये एक J E E Advanced level problem है जो formal charge को resonance से जोड़ता है। Azide ion linear और symmetric है, और हमें एक low formal charge structure बनानी है, charges assign करने हैं, और resonance से दोनों nitrogen nitrogen bond orders और lengths predict करने हैं।
पहले electron count। तीन nitrogens fifteen देते हैं, और single negative charge एक जोड़ता है, कुल sixteen valence electrons।

सबसे कम formal charge वाली linear structure central nitrogen पर दो nitrogen nitrogen double bonds रखती है, हर terminal nitrogen पर two lone pairs और centre पर कोई नहीं। पूरी चीज़ को overall minus one charge के साथ bracket में बनाइए।

Formal charges के लिए, V हर जगह five है। Central nitrogen पर कोई lone pair नहीं और इसके दो double bonds से eight bonding electrons हैं, तो इसका formal charge है five minus zero minus four, यानी plus one।

हर terminal nitrogen पर four lone pair electrons और four bonding electrons हैं, तो इसका formal charge है five minus four minus two, यानी minus one। Sum, minus one plus one minus one, equals minus one, जो ion के charge से match करता है। Structure सही है।

अब resonance। इस symmetric form का एक equivalent partner है जिसमें double bonds फिर से बँटकर एक तरफ़ triple bond और दूसरी तरफ़ single bond बन जाते हैं, और एक mirror image partner है जिसमें arrangement उलटा है।
चूँकि ये दोनों end on triple bond forms equivalent हैं और बराबर contribute करती हैं, real ion इन सबका symmetric blend है। हर nitrogen nitrogen linkage का average bond order दो हो जाता है।

और यहाँ resonance का deep lesson है: दोनों nitrogen nitrogen bonds length में identical हैं, ना कोई longer bond है ना shorter। Molecule एक single blended species है, chutney की तरह, ना कि किसी switch की तरह जो दो recipes के बीच flick करे, तो partial bond orders और equal bond lengths naturally निकल आते हैं, ऐसा conclusion जो कोई अकेली Lewis structure कभी नहीं दे सकती।

sections.title: Pitfalls and pro-tips: formal charge, Fajans, and polarity

board_events.text: The four slips that cost the most marks
Trap 1: confusing formal charge with oxidation number.
Trap 2: dropping the 1/2 on the bonding term.
Trap 3: treating 'many polar bonds' as 'polar molecule'.
Trap 4: inverting Fajans' logic.
Fajans mnemonic: 'SHaPe' -> Small, High charge, Pseudo-noble-gas.
Pro-tip: for polarity, sketch shape and look for symmetry.
Pro-tip: e x 100 pm approx 4.8 D; scale with bond length.

segments.text: Let us close subtopic one with the traps that repeatedly cost students marks, and the speed reflexes that save them.

First, do not confuse formal charge with oxidation number. Formal charge splits every shared pair equally, a covalent assumption, while oxidation number assigns both electrons to the more electronegative atom, an ionic assumption. The same atom can have a formal charge of zero and a non zero oxidation number.

Second, and this is the single most common formal charge slip, do not drop the half on the bonding term. A double bond contributes four shared electrons and a triple bond contributes six; forgetting to count both electrons of every pair, or forgetting to halve, wrecks the answer.

Third, never treat many polar bonds as automatically meaning a polar molecule. Carbon tetrachloride, carbon dioxide, and boron trifluoride are crammed with polar bonds yet are perfectly non polar. Always sum the bond dipoles as vectors and check the symmetry first.

Fourth, do not invert Fajans' logic. A small, highly charged cation paired with a large anion gives more covalent character, not more ionic. Students often memorise the factors but attach them to the wrong outcome.

A clean way to remember Fajans' factors for more covalent character is the mnemonic shape, spelled S H a P e: small cation, high charge, and pseudo noble gas configuration of the cation all push toward covalent character.

Now the pro tips. For any polarity question, never calculate. Sketch the shape and look for a centre of symmetry; if the molecule looks the same when you flip it, its dipole moment is almost certainly zero.

<whisper>And keep this yardstick ready.</whisper> For percentage ionic character, the electronic charge times one hundred picometres is about four point eight debye; scale it linearly with the bond length and you skip a whole slab of arithmetic under exam pressure.
चलिए subtopic one को उन traps के साथ बंद करते हैं जो बार बार students के marks खाते हैं, और उन speed reflexes के साथ जो उन्हें बचाते हैं।

पहला, formal charge को oxidation number से मत confuse कीजिए। Formal charge हर shared pair को बराबर बाँटता है, एक covalent assumption, जबकि oxidation number दोनों electrons को ज़्यादा electronegative atom को दे देता है, एक ionic assumption। एक ही atom का formal charge zero और oxidation number non zero हो सकता है।

दूसरा, और ये सबसे common formal charge slip है, bonding term पर half मत छोड़िए। एक double bond four shared electrons देता है और triple bond six; हर pair के दोनों electrons गिनना भूलना, या half करना भूलना, answer बिगाड़ देता है।

तीसरा, कभी भी कई polar bonds को अपने आप polar molecule का मतलब मत समझिए। Carbon tetrachloride, carbon dioxide, और boron trifluoride polar bonds से भरे हैं फिर भी perfectly non polar हैं। हमेशा bond dipoles को vectors की तरह जोड़िए और पहले symmetry check कीजिए।

चौथा, Fajans' logic को उलटिए मत। एक small, highly charged cation एक large anion के साथ ज़्यादा covalent character देता है, ज़्यादा ionic नहीं। Students अक्सर factors याद कर लेते हैं पर उन्हें ग़लत outcome से जोड़ देते हैं।

Fajans' factors को ज़्यादा covalent character के लिए याद रखने का साफ़ तरीक़ा है mnemonic shape, spelled S H a P e: small cation, high charge, और cation का pseudo noble gas configuration सब covalent character की ओर धकेलते हैं।
अब pro tips। किसी भी polarity question में कभी calculate मत कीजिए। Shape बनाइए और centre of symmetry ढूँढिए; अगर molecule flip करने पर same दिखे, तो इसका dipole moment लगभग यक़ीनन zero है।

<whisper>और ये yardstick तैयार रखिए।</whisper> Percentage ionic character के लिए, electronic charge times one hundred picometres लगभग four point eight debye होता है; इसे bond length के साथ linearly scale कीजिए और exam pressure में आप arithmetic का एक पूरा हिस्सा छोड़ देते हैं।

board_events.text: Four people in a lift move to the four corners.
A lone pair is a person with a wide suitcase: occupies more room.
Repulsion order: lp-lp > lp-bp > bp-bp.
Water's two lone pairs squeeze the angle to 104.5 degrees.
VSEPR gives shape, but is silent on why bonds form.

segments.text: <curious>A Lewis structure tells you who is bonded to whom, but it is flat and lifeless; it says nothing about the shape a molecule takes in three dimensions.</curious> Why is water bent and not straight? Why is methane a little tetrahedron and not a flat plus sign? The first theory to answer is V S E P R.

V S E P R stands for valence shell electron pair repulsion, and its whole idea fits in one sentence: the electron pairs around the central atom hate each other and spread out as far apart as they possibly can.

Think of helium balloons tied together at their knots. Tie two and they point opposite ways, a straight line. Tie three and they splay into a flat triangle. Tie four and they cannot stay flat; they bulge into a three dimensional tetrahedron. The balloons are the electron pairs, and their mutual avoidance is the molecular shape.

Here is the same idea with people. Imagine four people forced into a small lift, each wanting maximum personal space; they instinctively move to the four corners, never two crowding one side. Electron pairs do exactly this, except in three dimensions.

Now the twist that explains real molecules. A lone pair is like a person carrying a wide suitcase; it occupies more room and elbows the bonded pairs closer together. This is why water's bond angle of one hundred four point five degrees is squeezed below the ideal tetrahedral value.

The exact ranking to memorise is the repulsion order. Lone pair to lone pair repulsion is strongest, then lone pair to bond pair, and bond pair to bond pair is weakest. This single ordering explains every bond angle distortion in the chapter.

So oxygen's two lone suitcases push its two oxygen hydrogen bonds inward, dragging the angle from the ideal one hundred nine point five degrees down to one hundred four point five. That is the entire engine of V S E P R at work.
V S E P R is powerful but limited. It gives shape, yet it is completely silent on why a bond forms at all, and on why bonds differ in strength. For that we need the next theory, valence bond theory.

<curious>एक Lewis structure बताती है कौन किससे bonded है, पर वो flat और lifeless है; ये कुछ नहीं बताती कि molecule three dimensions में कौन सी shape लेता है।</curious> Water bent क्यों है, straight क्यों नहीं? Methane एक छोटा tetrahedron क्यों है, flat plus sign क्यों नहीं? पहला theory जो जवाब देता है वो है V S E P R।

V S E P R का मतलब है valence shell electron pair repulsion, और इसका पूरा idea एक sentence में आ जाता है: central atom के चारों ओर electron pairs एक दूसरे से नफ़रत करते हैं और जितना दूर हो सके उतना फैल जाते हैं।

Helium balloons को उनकी गाँठ पर बँधा हुआ सोचिए। दो बाँधिए और वो opposite दिशाओं में point करते हैं, एक straight line। तीन बाँधिए और वो एक flat triangle में फैल जाते हैं। चार बाँधिए और वो flat नहीं रह सकते; वो एक three dimensional tetrahedron में उभर आते हैं। Balloons ही electron pairs हैं, और उनका आपसी बचाव ही molecular shape है।

यही idea लोगों के साथ। सोचिए चार लोग एक छोटी lift में हैं, हर कोई ज़्यादा से ज़्यादा personal space चाहता है; वो instinctively चारों corners में चले जाते हैं, कभी दो एक तरफ़ भीड़ नहीं करते। Electron pairs बिलकुल यही करते हैं, बस three dimensions में।

अब वो twist जो real molecules समझाता है। एक lone pair एक ऐसे इंसान की तरह है जो चौड़ा suitcase लिए हो; वो ज़्यादा जगह घेरता है और bonded pairs को पास धकेल देता है। इसीलिए water का bond angle one hundred four point five degrees ideal tetrahedral value से नीचे दब जाता है।

याद रखने वाली exact ranking है repulsion order। Lone pair से lone pair repulsion सबसे strong, फिर lone pair से bond pair, और bond pair से bond pair सबसे weak। यही एक ordering chapter की हर bond angle distortion समझा देती है।

तो oxygen के दो lone suitcases इसके दो oxygen hydrogen bonds को अंदर की ओर धकेलते हैं, angle को ideal one hundred nine point five degrees से घटाकर one hundred four point five तक ले आते हैं। यही V S E P R का पूरा engine काम करते हुए है।
V S E P R powerful है पर limited। ये shape देता है, फिर भी बिलकुल silent है कि bond बनता ही क्यों है, और bonds strength में अलग क्यों होते हैं। इसके लिए हमें अगला theory चाहिए, valence bond theory।

sections.title: Valence bond theory and the need for hybridisation

board_events.text: A bond as overlapping orbitals
Sigma = firm handshake; pi = brushing fingertips.
Raw VBT predicts the wrong shapes (90 degrees for carbon).
The fix: hybridisation blends orbitals before bonding.
One s + three p -> four sp3 orbitals -> tetrahedron.
Limitation: VBT cannot explain O2's paramagnetism.
Hybridisation is bookkeeping we invoke after knowing geometry.

segments.text: Valence bond theory says a covalent bond forms when two atoms come close enough that their atomic orbitals overlap, and the more they overlap, the stronger the bond.

Think of two people shaking hands. A firm, full palm grip, which is head on overlap, gives a sigma bond and is far stronger than two people merely brushing fingertips sideways, which is sidewise overlap and gives a pi bond.

But raw valence bond theory predicts the wrong shapes. Pure atomic orbitals point along fixed axes, so carbon's bonds should be at ninety degrees, yet methane's bonds are at one hundred nine point five degrees and all four are identical. Something is missing.
The fix is hybridisation. Before bonding, the central atom blends its valence orbitals into a new set of equivalent hybrid orbitals that point in exactly the directions V S E P R demands.

Blending one s orbital with three p orbitals, which we write s p three, gives four identical orbitals aimed at the corners of a tetrahedron, and methane's shape falls out perfectly. Hybridisation is the bridge that makes valence bond theory agree with the shapes V S E P R predicts.

Valence bond theory and hybridisation are powerful for main group molecules, but they become strained for electron deficient species like diborane, and they cannot explain the paramagnetism of oxygen. That failure will force us into molecular orbital theory in the next subtopic.

One honest caution: hybridisation is a model we invoke after we already know the geometry, not a physical event the atom actually performs. Treat it as bookkeeping that happens to predict correctly, and you will never over interpret it.
Valence bond theory कहती है कि covalent bond तब बनता है जब दो atoms इतने पास आ जाएँ कि उनके atomic orbitals overlap करें, और जितना ज़्यादा वो overlap करें, bond उतना ही strong।

दो लोगों के हाथ मिलाने के बारे में सोचिए। एक firm, full palm grip, जो head on overlap है, sigma bond देता है और उन दो लोगों से कहीं ज़्यादा strong है जो बस उँगलियाँ बग़ल से छू रहे हों, जो sidewise overlap है और pi bond देता है।

पर raw valence bond theory ग़लत shapes predict करती है। Pure atomic orbitals fixed axes के साथ point करते हैं, तो carbon के bonds ninety degrees पर होने चाहिए, फिर भी methane के bonds one hundred nine point five degrees पर हैं और चारों identical हैं। कुछ missing है।

इसका fix है hybridisation। Bonding से पहले, central atom अपने valence orbitals को equivalent hybrid orbitals के एक नए set में blend कर देता है जो ठीक उन directions में point करते हैं जो V S E P R माँगता है।

एक s orbital को तीन p orbitals के साथ blend करना, जिसे हम s p three लिखते हैं, चार identical orbitals देता है जो एक tetrahedron के corners की ओर तने होते हैं, और methane की shape perfectly निकल आती है। Hybridisation वो bridge है जो valence bond theory को V S E P R की predict की shapes से सहमत करता है।

Valence bond theory और hybridisation main group molecules के लिए powerful हैं, पर diborane जैसी electron deficient species के लिए strained हो जाते हैं, और oxygen की paramagnetism नहीं समझा पाते। यही failure हमें अगले subtopic में molecular orbital theory की ओर धकेलेगी।

एक honest caution: hybridisation एक model है जिसे हम geometry पहले से जानने के बाद invoke करते हैं, ना कि कोई physical event जो atom असल में करता हो। इसे ऐसी bookkeeping मानिए जो सही predict कर देती है, और आप इसे कभी over interpret नहीं करेंगे।

sections.title: Steric number, hybridisation and the geometry table

board_events.text: The one count that fixes everything

board_events.latex: SN = (\text{sigma-bonded atoms}) + (\text{lone pairs on central atom})

board_events.text: H value maps: 2->sp, 3->sp2, 4->sp3, 5->sp3d, 6->sp3d2.
SN 2/3/4/5/6 -> linear/trigonal/tetrahedral/bipyramidal/octahedral.
More s-character -> larger angle, shorter stronger bond.
Sigma: head-on overlap; pi: sidewise overlap of unhybridised p.

segments.text: The whole of V S E P R and hybridisation runs on one count, the steric number. Get it right and shape, hybridisation, and ideal angle all follow automatically.

The steric number is the count of sigma bonded atoms plus the number of lone pairs on the central atom. Notice you count each multiple bond as just one region, one sigma, because for shape purposes a double or triple bond still occupies a single direction.

For a central atom surrounded by monovalent atoms there is a fast formula. H equals half the quantity V plus M minus C plus A, where V is the valence electrons of the central atom, M the number of monovalent atoms attached, C the positive charge, and A the negative charge.

The result maps straight to hybridisation. Two gives s p, three gives s p two, four gives s p three, five gives s p three d, and six gives s p three d two. Both routes, the steric number and this formula, count the same thing, because every sigma bond and every lone pair needs its own hybrid orbital to live in.

The steric number then sets the electron pair geometry and its ideal angle. Two is linear at one hundred eighty degrees, three is trigonal planar at one hundred twenty, four is tetrahedral at one hundred nine point five, five is trigonal bipyramidal with ninety and one hundred twenty degree angles, and six is octahedral at ninety degrees.

One more parameter matters, the percentage s character: s p is fifty percent, s p two is thirty three point three, and s p three is twenty five percent. More s character means a larger bond angle and a shorter, stronger bond, because s orbitals sit closer to the nucleus.

Finally the sigma versus pi distinction in bond counting. A sigma bond forms by head on overlap along the internuclear axis and is stronger; a pi bond forms by sidewise overlap of unhybridised p orbitals. A single bond is one sigma, a double is one sigma plus one pi, and a triple is one sigma plus two pi.
पूरा V S E P R और hybridisation एक count पर चलता है, steric number। इसे सही निकालिए और shape, hybridisation, और ideal angle सब अपने आप निकल आते हैं।

Steric number sigma bonded atoms की गिनती plus central atom पर lone pairs की संख्या है। ध्यान दीजिए हर multiple bond को सिर्फ़ एक region गिनते हैं, एक sigma, क्योंकि shape के लिए double या triple bond भी एक ही direction घेरता है।

Monovalent atoms से घिरे central atom के लिए एक तेज़ formula है। H equals half the quantity V plus M minus C plus A, जहाँ V central atom के valence electrons, M जुड़े monovalent atoms की संख्या, C positive charge, और A negative charge है।

नतीजा सीधे hybridisation से map होता है। Two देता है s p, three देता है s p two, four देता है s p three, five देता है s p three d, और six देता है s p three d two। दोनों routes, steric number और ये formula, एक ही चीज़ गिनते हैं, क्योंकि हर sigma bond और हर lone pair को अपना hybrid orbital चाहिए जिसमें वो रहे।

फिर steric number electron pair geometry और उसका ideal angle तय करता है। Two linear है one hundred eighty degrees पर, three trigonal planar one hundred twenty पर, four tetrahedral one hundred nine point five पर, five trigonal bipyramidal ninety और one hundred twenty degree angles के साथ, और six octahedral ninety degrees पर।

एक और parameter मायने रखता है, percentage s character: s p fifty percent है, s p two thirty three point three, और s p three twenty five percent। ज़्यादा s character का मतलब बड़ा bond angle और छोटा, strong bond, क्योंकि s orbitals nucleus के ज़्यादा क़रीब बैठते हैं।

आख़िर में bond counting में sigma versus pi का फ़र्क़। Sigma bond internuclear axis के साथ head on overlap से बनता है और stronger है; pi bond unhybridised p orbitals के sidewise overlap से बनता है। Single bond one sigma है, double one sigma plus one pi, और triple one sigma plus two pi।

sections.title: Predicting molecular shape with VSEPR, step by step

board_events.text: Electron geometry first, molecular shape second
Step 1-2: Draw Lewis, find central atom, compute SN.
Step 3: Read electron-pair geometry from SN.
Step 4: Subtract lone pairs to get the molecular SHAPE.
Step 5: Adjust angles using the repulsion order.
Ammonia: SN=4, one lone pair -> trigonal pyramidal, 107 degrees.
Water: SN=4, two lone pairs -> bent, 104.5 degrees.

segments.text: The single trickiest thing in V S E P R is keeping two ideas separate: the electron pair geometry, which counts all pairs, and the molecular shape, which counts atoms only. Here is the procedure that keeps them straight.

Steps one and two: draw the Lewis structure, identify the central atom, and compute the steric number as sigma bonds plus lone pairs, treating each multiple bond as a single region of electron density.
Step three: read off the electron pair geometry from the steric number using the table. This is the arrangement of all the electron pairs, both bonding and lone.

Step four, the crucial one: subtract the lone pairs to get the molecular shape, the arrangement of the atoms only. The lone pairs are still there distorting things, they just are not part of the named shape.

Step five: adjust the bond angles using the repulsion order. Each lone pair squeezes the bond angles below the ideal value, because a lone pair is held by only one nucleus, so its cloud is fatter and pushes harder than a bond pair shared between two nuclei.

Take ammonia. It has steric number four, three nitrogen hydrogen bonds plus one lone pair, so its electron geometry is tetrahedral, but with one lone pair the actual shape is trigonal pyramidal, and the angle is squeezed to one hundred seven degrees from the ideal one hundred nine point five.

Water goes further. Same steric number four, but now two lone pairs, so the shape is bent and the angle is squeezed all the way to one hundred four point five degrees. Two suitcases squeeze harder than one, exactly as the repulsion order predicts.
V S E P R में सबसे tricky चीज़ है दो ideas को अलग रखना: electron pair geometry, जो सारे pairs गिनती है, और molecular shape, जो सिर्फ़ atoms गिनती है। यहाँ वो procedure है जो इन्हें साफ़ रखता है।
Steps one और two: Lewis structure बनाइए, central atom पहचानिए, और steric number निकालिए sigma bonds plus lone pairs के रूप में, हर multiple bond को electron density का एक single region मानते हुए।
Step three: steric number से table का इस्तेमाल करके electron pair geometry पढ़िए। ये सारे electron pairs का arrangement है, bonding और lone दोनों।
Step four, सबसे ज़रूरी: lone pairs घटाइए ताकि molecular shape मिले, सिर्फ़ atoms का arrangement। Lone pairs अभी भी वहाँ हैं चीज़ों को distort करते हुए, वो बस named shape का हिस्सा नहीं हैं।

Step five: repulsion order का इस्तेमाल करके bond angles adjust कीजिए। हर lone pair bond angles को ideal value से नीचे दबाता है, क्योंकि lone pair सिर्फ़ एक nucleus पकड़ता है, तो इसका cloud मोटा होता है और दो nuclei के बीच बँटे bond pair से ज़्यादा ज़ोर से धकेलता है।

Ammonia लीजिए। इसका steric number four है, तीन nitrogen hydrogen bonds plus one lone pair, तो इसकी electron geometry tetrahedral है, पर one lone pair के साथ असली shape trigonal pyramidal है, और angle ideal one hundred nine point five से दबकर one hundred seven degrees हो जाता है।

Water और आगे जाता है। वही steric number four, पर अब two lone pairs, तो shape bent है और angle पूरे one hundred four point five degrees तक दब जाता है। दो suitcases एक से ज़्यादा ज़ोर से दबाते हैं, बिलकुल जैसा repulsion order predict करता है।

board_events.text: Carbon promotes one 2s electron, then hybridises.
Ethane: sp3 carbon, C-C single, ~154 pm, freely rotating.
Ethene: sp2 carbon, C=C is one sigma + one pi, ~134 pm, flat.
Ethyne: sp carbon, C-triple-C is one sigma + two pi, shortest.
Down the ladder: s-character up, length down, strength up.

segments.text: Before the ladder, one foundational picture. Valence bond theory begins with the hydrogen molecule: as two atoms approach, the attraction between each nucleus and the other's electron grows faster than the repulsions, so the potential energy falls to a minimum.

That energy minimum is the bond. For hydrogen it sits at an internuclear separation of seventy four picometres, the hydrogen hydrogen bond length, and the depth of the well is four hundred thirty five point eight kilojoules per mole, released as the bond forms.

Now carbon. Its ground state has only two unpaired electrons, predicting two bonds at ninety degrees, which contradicts methane. The resolution: one two s electron is promoted to the empty two p orbital, giving four unpaired electrons, and then the one s and three p orbitals hybridise. The small promotion cost is repaid many times over by forming four strong bonds instead of two.

Now the ladder. In ethane each carbon is s p three, mixing one s with three p into four hybrids. One hybrid on each carbon overlaps head on for the carbon carbon sigma bond, and the others bond to hydrogen. There are no leftover p orbitals, so the linkage is a single bond, about one hundred fifty four picometres long, and freely rotating.

In ethene each carbon is s p two, three hybrids in a plane at about one hundred twenty degrees, with one unhybridised p orbital perpendicular. The hybrids form the sigma framework and the two perpendicular p orbitals overlap sidewise into one pi bond. So the double bond is one sigma plus one pi, the length contracts to about one hundred thirty four picometres, and the pi bond makes ethene flat and locks it against rotation.

In ethyne each carbon is s p, two hybrids pointing one hundred eighty degrees apart, leaving two unhybridised p orbitals. The hybrids form the sigma bonds and the two pairs of perpendicular p orbitals form two pi bonds. So the triple bond is one sigma plus two pi, and it is the shortest of the three.

<excited>Read the ladder top to bottom and one clean trend ties it all together.</excited> The s character rises from twenty five to thirty three to fifty percent, the bond length shrinks from one hundred fifty four to one hundred thirty four to about one hundred twenty picometres, and the bond strength climbs, linking hybridisation, geometry, and bond parameters in a single story.

Ladder से पहले एक foundational picture। Valence bond theory hydrogen molecule से शुरू होती है: जैसे दो atoms पास आते हैं, हर nucleus और दूसरे के electron के बीच attraction repulsions से तेज़ बढ़ता है, तो potential energy एक minimum तक गिरती है।

वो energy minimum ही bond है। Hydrogen के लिए ये seventy four picometres की internuclear separation पर बैठता है, hydrogen hydrogen bond length, और well की गहराई four hundred thirty five point eight kilojoules per mole है, जो bond बनते समय release होती है।

अब carbon। इसकी ground state में सिर्फ़ two unpaired electrons हैं, जो ninety degrees पर two bonds predict करते हैं, जो methane से मेल नहीं खाता। इसका हल: एक two s electron को empty two p orbital में promote किया जाता है, जिससे four unpaired electrons मिलते हैं, और फिर one s और three p orbitals hybridise हो जाते हैं। promotion की छोटी क़ीमत two की जगह four strong bonds बनाकर कई गुना वसूल हो जाती है।

अब ladder। Ethane में हर carbon s p three है, एक s को तीन p के साथ चार hybrids में मिलाता है। हर carbon पर एक hybrid carbon carbon sigma bond के लिए head on overlap करता है, और बाक़ी hydrogen से bond करते हैं। कोई leftover p orbitals नहीं, तो linkage single bond है, क़रीब one hundred fifty four picometres लंबा, और freely rotating।

Ethene में हर carbon s p two है, तीन hybrids एक plane में क़रीब one hundred twenty degrees पर, और एक unhybridised p orbital perpendicular। Hybrids sigma framework बनाते हैं और दो perpendicular p orbitals sidewise overlap करके एक pi bond बनाते हैं। तो double bond one sigma plus one pi है, length सिकुड़कर क़रीब one hundred thirty four picometres, और pi bond ethene को flat बनाकर rotation के ख़िलाफ़ lock कर देता है।

Ethyne में हर carbon s p है, दो hybrids one hundred eighty degrees की दूरी पर, दो unhybridised p orbitals छोड़ते हुए। Hybrids sigma bonds बनाते हैं और perpendicular p orbitals के दो जोड़े two pi bonds बनाते हैं। तो triple bond one sigma plus two pi है, और तीनों में सबसे छोटा है।

<excited>Ladder को ऊपर से नीचे पढ़िए और एक साफ़ trend सब कुछ जोड़ देता है।</excited> S character twenty five से thirty three से fifty percent तक बढ़ता है, bond length one hundred fifty four से one hundred thirty four से क़रीब one hundred twenty picometres तक सिकुड़ता है, और bond strength चढ़ता है, hybridisation, geometry, और bond parameters को एक ही कहानी में जोड़ते हुए।

sections.title: Worked examples: PCl3 shape and XeF2 hybridisation

board_events.text: Applying the steric number to two molecules
PCl3: P has 5 valence e-, three bonds, one lone pair.
SN = 3 + 1 = 4 -> tetrahedral electron geometry.
Shape: trigonal pyramidal, angle ~100 degrees.
XeF2: use H = 1/2[V + M - C + A].
Trap: seeing two bonds and rushing to sp. Always count lone pairs.

segments.text: Let us apply the procedure to two molecules, a C B S E shape question on phosphorus trichloride and a N E E T hybridisation trap on xenon difluoride.
For phosphorus trichloride, phosphorus is central with five valence electrons. It forms three phosphorus chlorine single bonds, using three electrons, and that leaves one lone pair on phosphorus.
The steric number is three sigma bonds plus one lone pair, which is four, so the electron pair geometry is tetrahedral.

Subtracting the one lone pair gives a trigonal pyramidal shape, just like ammonia. The lone pair repels the three bond pairs and squeezes the chlorine phosphorus chlorine angle a little below one hundred nine point five, to about one hundred degrees experimentally.
Now xenon difluoride, a speed trap. Use the hybridisation formula directly. For xenon, V is eight, M is two for the two fluorines, and both C and A are zero.

So H is half of eight plus two, which is five, giving s p three d hybridisation. The three lone pairs occupy the equatorial plane, and the molecule is linear, fluorine xenon fluorine in a straight line.

Here is the trap. Students see only two bonds and rush to s p, forgetting that xenon's three lone pairs also demand hybrid orbitals and count toward the steric number. The shape is linear, but the hybridisation is emphatically not s p; always include the lone pairs.
चलिए procedure को दो molecules पर लगाते हैं, phosphorus trichloride पर एक C B S E shape question और xenon difluoride पर एक N E E T hybridisation trap।
Phosphorus trichloride के लिए, phosphorus central है five valence electrons के साथ। ये तीन phosphorus chlorine single bonds बनाता है, तीन electrons use करके, और phosphorus पर one lone pair बचती है।
Steric number three sigma bonds plus one lone pair है, यानी four, तो electron pair geometry tetrahedral है।

एक lone pair घटाने पर trigonal pyramidal shape मिलती है, बिलकुल ammonia की तरह। Lone pair तीन bond pairs को धकेलती है और chlorine phosphorus chlorine angle को one hundred nine point five से थोड़ा नीचे दबा देती है, experimentally क़रीब one hundred degrees तक।
अब xenon difluoride, एक speed trap। Hybridisation formula सीधे use कीजिए। Xenon के लिए, V eight है, M दो fluorines के लिए two, और C और A दोनों zero।
तो H eight plus two का आधा है, यानी five, जो s p three d hybridisation देता है। तीन lone pairs equatorial plane घेरती हैं, और molecule linear है, fluorine xenon fluorine एक straight line में।

यहाँ trap है। Students सिर्फ़ two bonds देखकर s p की ओर दौड़ते हैं, ये भूलकर कि xenon की तीन lone pairs भी hybrid orbitals माँगती हैं और steric number में गिनी जाती हैं। Shape linear है, पर hybridisation बिलकुल s p नहीं है; हमेशा lone pairs शामिल कीजिए।

board_events.text: See-saw is asymmetric, so bond dipoles do not cancel.
Answer: sp3d, see-saw, polar.

segments.text: This J E E Main problem links hybridisation, lone pair placement, and polarity all in one molecule, sulphur tetrafluoride. We find the hybridisation, the shape, and whether it is polar.

For sulphur, V is six and M is four, with no charge, so H is half of six plus four, which is five, giving s p three d. Equivalently the steric number is four sigma bonds plus one lone pair, also five.
So the electron pair geometry is trigonal bipyramidal, five regions of electron density arranged with three in an equatorial plane and two along the axis.

Now the key decision: where does the single lone pair go? It occupies an equatorial position, not axial. Why? An equatorial lone pair faces only two near neighbours at ninety degrees, whereas an axial one would face three at ninety degrees, a higher repulsion arrangement.

Removing that equatorial lone pair from the trigonal bipyramid leaves a see saw shape, with two axial fluorines bent slightly away from the fat lone pair cloud and two equatorial fluorines completing the figure.

Because the see saw shape is asymmetric, the four sulphur fluorine bond dipoles do not cancel, so sulphur tetrafluoride is polar. Contrast this with octahedral sulphur hexafluoride, which is perfectly symmetric and therefore non polar.

So the complete answer is s p three d hybridisation, a see saw molecular shape, and a polar molecule. The lesson worth carrying: lone pair placement in a trigonal bipyramid is always equatorial, and asymmetry from that lone pair is what makes see saw molecules polar.
ये J E E Main problem hybridisation, lone pair placement, और polarity तीनों को एक molecule में जोड़ता है, sulphur tetrafluoride। हम hybridisation, shape, और polarity तीनों निकालते हैं।
Sulphur के लिए, V six है और M four, बिना charge, तो H six plus four का आधा है, यानी five, जो s p three d देता है। इसी तरह steric number four sigma bonds plus one lone pair है, वो भी five।
तो electron pair geometry trigonal bipyramidal है, electron density के पाँच regions, तीन equatorial plane में और दो axis के साथ।

अब key decision: अकेली lone pair कहाँ जाती है? ये equatorial position घेरती है, axial नहीं। क्यों? एक equatorial lone pair सिर्फ़ two near neighbours का सामना ninety degrees पर करती है, जबकि axial वाली तीन का सामना ninety degrees पर करती, एक higher repulsion arrangement।
Trigonal bipyramid से वो equatorial lone pair हटाने पर एक see saw shape बचती है, दो axial fluorines मोटे lone pair cloud से थोड़ा दूर झुके हुए और दो equatorial fluorines figure पूरा करते हुए।

चूँकि see saw shape asymmetric है, चारों sulphur fluorine bond dipoles cancel नहीं होते, तो sulphur tetrafluoride polar है। इसकी तुलना octahedral sulphur hexafluoride से कीजिए, जो perfectly symmetric है और इसलिए non polar।

तो पूरा answer है s p three d hybridisation, एक see saw molecular shape, और एक polar molecule। साथ ले जाने लायक़ lesson: trigonal bipyramid में lone pair placement हमेशा equatorial होती है, और उसी lone pair से आई asymmetry ही see saw molecules को polar बनाती है।

sections.subtopic: VSEPR Theory, Valence Bond Theory & Hybridization
sections.title: Worked example: bond angle order in H2O, H2S, H2Se

board_events.text: Same hybridisation, very different angles
All three are sp3 (SN=4), all bent.
Angles: H2O 104.5, H2S ~92, H2Se ~91 degrees.
Argument 1: central-atom electronegativity falls down the group.
As centre gets less electronegative, angle collapses toward 90.
Argument 2: heavier hydrides bond with more p-character.
Answer: H2O > H2S > H2Se. Same hybridisation, not same angle.

segments.text: This J E E Advanced problem asks us to arrange water, hydrogen sulphide, and hydrogen selenide in decreasing order of their hydrogen central atom hydrogen bond angle, and to justify it with two distinct arguments.

First note what they share. All three have steric number four, two bonds plus two lone pairs, so all three are s p three and all three are bent. Yet the experimental angles fall sharply from water down to selenide.

The numbers are striking: water is one hundred four point five degrees, hydrogen sulphide about ninety two, and hydrogen selenide about ninety one, hugging a right angle. Identical hybridisation, and yet a fourteen degree spread. Two arguments explain it.

Argument one, electronegativity. Down the group from oxygen to sulphur to selenium, the central atom's electronegativity falls. A more electronegative centre like oxygen pulls the bonding pairs closer to itself, so they sit nearer together and repel harder, propping the angle open.
As the central atom becomes less electronegative, the bonding pairs drift outward, repel less, and the angle collapses toward ninety degrees. That is exactly the trend from oxygen down to selenium.

Argument two, orbital character. In the heavier hydrides the central atom uses orbitals with less s character in bonding, closer to pure p, and pure p orbitals are mutually ninety degrees. Oxygen retains more s character in its bonds, holding the angle well above ninety, while selenium's near pure p bonding pushes it almost to ninety.

So the order is water, then hydrogen sulphide, then hydrogen selenide. The deep point to carry away: identical hybridisation does not mean identical bond angle; central atom electronegativity and effective s character fine tune the value, and the trend is smoothly downward all the way down the group.

ये J E E Advanced problem हमसे कहता है कि water, hydrogen sulphide, और hydrogen selenide को उनके hydrogen central atom hydrogen bond angle के घटते क्रम में लगाएँ, और इसे दो अलग arguments से justify करें।

पहले देखिए इनमें common क्या है। तीनों का steric number four है, two bonds plus two lone pairs, तो तीनों s p three हैं और तीनों bent हैं। फिर भी experimental angles water से selenide तक तेज़ी से गिरते हैं।

Numbers चौंकाने वाले हैं: water one hundred four point five degrees, hydrogen sulphide क़रीब ninety two, और hydrogen selenide क़रीब ninety one, एक right angle के पास। Identical hybridisation, फिर भी fourteen degree का फ़ैलाव। दो arguments इसे समझाते हैं।

Argument one, electronegativity। Group में oxygen से sulphur से selenium नीचे जाते हुए, central atom की electronegativity गिरती है। oxygen जैसा ज़्यादा electronegative centre bonding pairs को अपने पास खींचता है, तो वो पास बैठकर ज़्यादा ज़ोर से repel करते हैं, angle को खुला रखते हुए।
जैसे central atom कम electronegative होता है, bonding pairs बाहर की ओर सरकते हैं, कम repel करते हैं, और angle ninety degrees की ओर गिरता है। यही ठीक वो trend है oxygen से selenium तक।

Argument two, orbital character। भारी hydrides में central atom bonding में कम s character वाले orbitals use करता है, pure p के ज़्यादा क़रीब, और pure p orbitals आपस में ninety degrees होते हैं। Oxygen अपने bonds में ज़्यादा s character रखता है, angle को ninety से काफ़ी ऊपर पकड़े हुए, जबकि selenium की near pure p bonding इसे लगभग ninety तक धकेल देती है।

तो order है water, फिर hydrogen sulphide, फिर hydrogen selenide। साथ ले जाने वाला deep point: identical hybridisation का मतलब identical bond angle नहीं; central atom electronegativity और effective s character value को fine tune करते हैं, और trend group में पूरे नीचे तक smoothly गिरता जाता है।

sections.subtopic: VSEPR Theory, Valence Bond Theory & Hybridization
sections.title: Pitfalls and pro-tips: VSEPR and hybridisation

board_events.text: Four traps between you and full marks
Trap 1: confusing electron-pair geometry with molecular shape.
Trap 2: dropping lone pairs from the steric number.
Trap 3: assuming same hybridisation means same bond angle.
Trap 4: muddling sigma and pi overlap.
Pro-tip: one glance at steric number gives hybridisation and geometry.
Pro-tip: two shrinking forces on bond angle.

segments.text: Let us close subtopic two with the recurring V S E P R and hybridisation traps, and two speed reflexes that win marks quickly.

First, do not confuse electron pair geometry with molecular shape. Water is tetrahedral in electron geometry but bent in shape. The named shape counts atoms only; the lone pairs distort everything but are invisible in the shape's name.

Second, never drop lone pairs from the steric number. Counting only bonded atoms makes xenon difluoride look s p and sulphur tetrafluoride look s p three. Every lone pair occupies a hybrid orbital and must be counted.

Third, do not assume the same hybridisation means the same bond angle. Water, hydrogen sulphide, and hydrogen selenide are all s p three yet span one hundred four point five degrees down to about ninety one. Hybridisation sets the ideal angle; electronegativity and lone pairs fine tune the real one.
Fourth, do not muddle sigma and pi overlap. A sigma bond is head on along the axis; a pi bond is sidewise. Only unhybridised p orbitals form pi bonds, and sigma is always the stronger of the two.

Now the pro tips. For any main group molecule, compute the steric number in one glance, count atoms bonded to the centre and add the lone pairs, and you instantly have both the hybridisation and the electron geometry.

<whisper>For bond angle comparisons, remember two shrinking forces.</whisper> More lone pairs shrink the angle, and a less electronegative central atom shrinks it too. Spot which force is in play and the ordering falls out immediately.
चलिए subtopic two को बार बार आने वाले V S E P R और hybridisation traps के साथ बंद करते हैं, और दो speed reflexes के साथ जो तेज़ी से marks दिलाते हैं।

पहला, electron pair geometry को molecular shape से मत confuse कीजिए। Water electron geometry में tetrahedral है पर shape में bent। Named shape सिर्फ़ atoms गिनती है; lone pairs सब कुछ distort करती हैं पर shape के नाम में दिखती नहीं।

दूसरा, steric number से lone pairs कभी मत छोड़िए। सिर्फ़ bonded atoms गिनने से xenon difluoride s p दिखता है और sulphur tetrafluoride s p three। हर lone pair एक hybrid orbital घेरती है और गिनी जानी चाहिए।

तीसरा, ये मत मानिए कि same hybridisation का मतलब same bond angle। Water, hydrogen sulphide, और hydrogen selenide सब s p three हैं फिर भी one hundred four point five degrees से क़रीब ninety one तक फैले हैं। Hybridisation ideal angle तय करती है; electronegativity और lone pairs असली को fine tune करते हैं।
चौथा, sigma और pi overlap को मत गड्डमड्ड कीजिए। Sigma bond axis के साथ head on है; pi bond sidewise। सिर्फ़ unhybridised p orbitals pi bonds बनाते हैं, और sigma दोनों में हमेशा strong है।
अब pro tips। किसी भी main group molecule के लिए, steric number एक नज़र में निकालिए, centre से bonded atoms गिनिए और lone pairs जोड़िए, और आपके पास तुरंत hybridisation और electron geometry दोनों हैं।

<whisper>Bond angle की तुलना के लिए, दो shrinking forces याद रखिए।</whisper> ज़्यादा lone pairs angle को छोटा करती हैं, और कम electronegative central atom भी इसे छोटा करता है। पहचानिए कौन सी force काम कर रही है और ordering तुरंत निकल आती है।
